name: Plan platform local unlock support
description:
Design fd0 platform-local biometric/user-presence unlock end to end before implementation.

Goal:
Add a new fd0 auth method for local OS-protected unlock, covering macOS Touch ID/Secure Enclave or Keychain first and Linux/Framework Laptop via fprintd/PAM/Secret Service where possible. This must be a real auth method that unwraps fd0 K_unlock and super_priv through the existing user-chain/vault-wrap architecture, not a UI-only prompt in front of an already-available secret.

Core architecture requirement:
fd0-agent remains the single local unlock authority. CLI and future GUI both talk to the agent. The GUI may trigger native OS UI, but it must not become a second vault implementation and should not receive K_unlock, payload_key, or super_priv. If a platform needs foreground/UI process semantics, use an agent-owned helper or explicit security decision rather than silently moving secrets into the GUI.

Current architecture facts:
- User chain auth.set entries carry method_id, method_type, public_params, encrypted_super_priv.
- Vault wrapped_payload_keys carry method_id, method_type, public_params, wrap_nonce, wrapped.
- Existing method types are passphrase and yubikey.
- Passphrase derives K_unlock from Argon2id params.
- YubiKey stores a random K_unlock sealed to a hardware key and uses that K_unlock to decrypt encrypted_super_priv and vault payload_key.
- Server mostly stores signed opaque events; protocol-visible method_type/public_params changes affect clients, not server DB semantics.

Recommended protocol shape:
- Add method_type = platform-local, not fingerprint. Fingerprint is one possible local authentication policy; the useful primitive is a device-local OS protected secret released after user presence/biometric/system auth.
- public_params should be deterministic CBOR: PlatformLocalPublicParams { version, provider, key_ref, policy, flags }. Keep it minimal and non-secret.
- encrypted_super_priv remains unchanged: AEAD(K_unlock, super_priv, existing AAD).
- vault wrap remains unchanged: K_unlock wraps payload_key like other methods.

Provider model:
- macos-keychain-touchid: store/retrieve random 32-byte K_unlock in Keychain with LocalAuthentication access control requiring biometrics or device-owner auth.
- linux-secretservice-fprintd: verify user through fprintd/PAM, then retrieve random 32-byte K_unlock from Secret Service/KWallet/GNOME Keyring or a backend explicitly documented as local-user-session protected. This is weaker than Secure Enclave; document as OS-trust + biometric gate.
- Future providers can include windows-hello, tpm2, passkey/platform authenticator.

Non-goals for first implementation:
- Do not make biometric data part of cryptographic derivation. Fingerprints are not secrets and cannot be rotated.
- Do not support cross-device portability. This auth method is per-device; recovery/passphrase/YubiKey remains required.
- Do not allow platform-local as the only auth method unless recovery/export exists and UX explicitly confirms risk. Prefer requiring an existing unlocked session to enroll it.

Acceptance criteria for final implementation:
- docs/PROTOCOL.md updated with method_type, public_params CDDL, security semantics, client compatibility.
- internal/proto has PlatformLocalPublicParams and tests/golden compatibility.
- vault has PlatformLocalResolver with provider interface and strict validation.
- agent wire supports method_type platform-local without smuggling unrelated credentials.
- agent exposes a shared CLI/GUI-safe RPC/capability surface for platform-local unlock.
- CLI supports auth add --platform-local and unlock --method=platform-local with clear errors and fallback guidance.
- Future GUI can unlock through fd0-agent without handling raw K_unlock/super_priv.
- macOS provider has real Keychain/LocalAuthentication implementation or build-tagged stub with tests.
- Linux provider has fprintd/PAM preflight and a deliberate secret-backend decision before implementation.
- doctor reports platform-local method health: provider available, key_ref exists, policy readable where possible.
- tests cover unknown old clients failing clearly, bad public_params, missing key_ref, wrong provider, resolver returning bad K_unlock length, enrollment rollback atomicity.
- docs explain security: convenience unlock, device-local, OS trust boundary, never sole recovery.
result: Implemented platform-local auth end to end. Added method_type=platform-local and PlatformLocalPublicParams; vault resolver; agent unlock routing with no credential payload; CLI auth add/unlock UX; doctor structural checks; provider dispatcher; dev-local isolated test provider; macOS provider using LocalAuthentication user presence before device-local Keychain lookup; Linux provider using fprintd-verify plus Secret Service via secret-tool; best-effort provider cleanup on auth rm; protocol/threat docs and safe local scripts. Automated verification: go test ./..., go run ./tools/threat-coverage, git diff --check, bash tests/integration_platform_local.sh, macOS Keychain store/delete smoke, Linux cross-compile for platformauth/fd0/fd0-agent, manual provider scripts skip unless explicitly opted in. Manual hardware/UI smoke remains opt-in: FD0_PLATFORM_LOCAL_MACOS_MANUAL=1 bash tests/manual_platform_macos.sh and FD0_PLATFORM_LOCAL_LINUX_MANUAL=1 bash tests/manual_platform_linux.sh.

name: Wave D: VerifiedSTH type-state for verify-before-commit
description:
Type-state pattern: a translog.STH can ONLY be persisted into the vault
after passing VerifyAndCrossCheck. Currently this is a runtime
assertion at every call site. Make it a compile-time guarantee.

Bug pattern this eliminates: "wrong ordering" (20% of all bugs) +
"persist before verify" subset of "missing check".

## Design

```go
// internal/cli/translog.go

// VerifiedSTH proves that an STH passed full server-pub +
// inclusion + consistency + (optional) witness cross-check.
// Constructible ONLY via VerifyAndCrossCheck.
type VerifiedSTH struct {
    // private fields — no other package can construct
    sth     translog.STH
    server  CanonicalURL
    chainID ScopeID
}

func (v *VerifiedSTH) STH() translog.STH { return v.sth }
func (v *VerifiedSTH) Encode() ([]byte, error) { ... }

// Returns *VerifiedSTH only if everything verifies.
func VerifyAndCrossCheck(...) (*VerifiedSTH, error)
```

Then ScopeData.LastSTH update only via:
```go
func (sd *ScopeData) PersistLastSTH(v *VerifiedSTH) {
    sd.LastSTH, _ = v.Encode()
}
```

Calling `sd.LastSTH = encodedRawSTH` becomes a private-field violation
(or we remove the public field entirely and force going through
PersistLastSTH).

## Acceptance

- VerifiedSTH cannot be constructed outside `cli` package
- Persist functions take *VerifiedSTH, not raw STH
- A test that tries to construct VerifiedSTH externally fails to compile
  (verified by running `go build ./...` after a deliberate violation)
- All tests green

## Bug classes eliminated

- sync.go:430 "push verify proves wrong event" — caller can no longer
  hand a raw STH past verify
- "Wrong ordering: persist before verify" — compile error

## Effort

1 day. Smaller refactor than Wave C.

## Dependencies

Should land AFTER Wave C (CanonicalURL + ScopeID feed VerifiedSTH).

name: Pure crypto layer: OpenSealedFromShared
description:
Goal: implement the post-ECDH portion of libsodium crypto_box_seal_open as a pure function that takes the ECDH shared secret as input. Verified against nacl/box's existing OpenAnonymous via property test.

Reference: nacl/box.OpenAnonymous (golang.org/x/crypto/nacl/box) is libsodium-compatible (already used by crypto.OpenAnonymous in internal/crypto/crypto.go). The construction:

  shared = X25519(card_priv, eph_pub)                 ; on-card step (input here)
  sym_key = HSalsa20(shared, zero_nonce)              ; nacl key-derive
  nonce = BLAKE2b-512(eph_pub || recipient_pub)[:24]
  plain = XSalsa20-Poly1305_open(ct, nonce, sym_key)

Steps:
1. internal/crypto/sealedbox.go: add OpenSealedFromShared(ephPub, recipientPub [32]byte, ct, shared []byte) ([]byte, bool). Returns plaintext + ok flag (matches existing OpenAnonymous signature).

2. Implementation: use golang.org/x/crypto/nacl/secretbox for the AEAD open (XSalsa20-Poly1305) and golang.org/x/crypto/salsa20/salsa for HSalsa20, and golang.org/x/crypto/blake2b for the nonce. (Same primitives nacl/box uses internally.)

3. Roundtrip property test (sealedbox_test.go):
   - Generate random recipient X25519 keypair.
   - SealAnonymous(plain, recipientPub) via existing crypto.SealAnonymous.
   - ParseSealed → eph_pub, ct.
   - shared = curve25519.X25519(recipientPriv, eph_pub).
   - plain' = OpenSealedFromShared(eph_pub, recipientPub, ct, shared).
   - Assert plain' == plain AND ok.
   - Run 200 random iterations.

4. Cross-check vectors: hard-code 3–5 sealed-box test vectors generated externally (e.g. via Python pynacl) into testdata/sealedbox_vectors.json. Includes (recipient_priv, recipient_pub, plaintext, sealed). Replay test verifies our open path on each.

5. Negative tests: tampered ct, wrong recipient pub, wrong shared, truncated input — all return ok=false.

Done when:
- OpenSealedFromShared passes 200-iter property test against existing OpenAnonymous.
- Cross-check vectors verify (proves we match libsodium, not just ourselves).
- All negative tests pass.
- Codex review confirms libsodium semantics match.
result: OpenSealedFromShared lands pure-software libsodium crypto_box_seal_open completion. HSalsa20 key derivation + BLAKE2b 24-byte nonce + XSalsa20-Poly1305 open. All-zero shared rejection at entry; Wipe()-with-KeepAlive on stack copies of shared and key. Both bool and err-returning variants. Tests: 200-iter property roundtrip vs nacl/box.OpenAnonymous, 3 frozen wire-format vectors, single-bit tamper anywhere in blob, wrong recipient pub, wrong shared, zero shared, bad-length shared, empty-plaintext edge case. Codex review 2 rounds, all P1/P2 resolved.

name: Harden platform-local auth for production
description: Fix the security review findings before platform-local auth is committed. Requirements: (1) prevent auth add/remove ReSeal failure from bricking unlock while preserving rollback protection: agent unlock may tolerate user-chain ahead only when the used wrap is still present in the latest signed auth.set and its encrypted_super_priv decrypts under the used K_unlock to the same super_priv; revoked/stale wraps must still be refused. (1) Agent unlock now tolerates a user-chain-ahead AuthTip only when the used wrap is still live in the latest signed auth.set and encrypted_super_priv decrypts under the used K_unlock to the same super_priv; revoked/stale wraps still fail. name: YubiKey sealed-box completion (no-hardware portion)
description:
Goal: do everything possible without a YubiKey now, so hardware day shrinks to 30min: connect card, run recorder, commit JSON.

Strategy: decompose the sealed-box open path so the hardware step is one isolated call:

  card.SharedSecret(ephPub) → shared

name: Wave F: Spec compliance test generator (optional)
description:
Optional / lower priority. Generate test stubs from PROTOCOL.md /
TRANSLOG.md / STORAGE.md / API.md MUST-clauses so spec drift fails

## Background

10% of bugs found were "spec drift" — implementation didn't match the
documented behavior. Examples:
- payload_key fresh-per-save promise vs SaveBody reuse
- nil vs empty bytes for genesis prev_hash
- /users events `since` inclusivity vs API.md spec

Most spec-drift bugs are catchable via "implementation matches doc"

Build `tools/spec-coverage/`:
1. Parse PROTOCOL.md / TRANSLOG.md / STORAGE.md / API.md.
2. Extract every MUST/SHOULD clause + its surrounding context.
3. Emit Go test stubs grouped by spec file + section.
4. Each stub has the spec quote as comment + a TODO assertion.

- Generated stubs have spec quotes as comments.
- Coverage report: # of MUSTs in spec / # with corresponding test.
- CI fails if any generated stub is empty (TODO assertion not filled in).

3-5 days. Markdown parsing + Go AST generation + initial fill-in of
the most security-critical assertions.

Lower priority — Waves A-E will reduce bug rate significantly already.
F is "long-tail spec drift". Reserve for v1.x.

name: Fix flaky arm64 website build in release-docker pipeline
description:
## Problem

The arm64 build of `fd0-website` in `.github/workflows/release-docker.yml` failed during the v0.0.4 release (run 27103973167). Job `fd0-website (arm64)` failed at the `docker/setup-qemu-action@v3` step, specifically the "Pulling binfmt Docker image" sub-step, with:

```
Error response from daemon: Get "https://registry-1.docker.io/v2/": context deadline exceeded
```

`fd0-website (amd64)` succeeded in the same run. `fd0-server` and `fd0-witness` arm64 builds were still queued at the time of the failure.

## Diagnosis

This is a transient Docker Hub timeout when pulling the binfmt qemu image needed for arm64 cross-compilation under emulation. The pipeline previously succeeded for v0.0.1 through v0.0.3, so the workflow itself isn't broken — it's the upstream registry timing out under load.

## Acceptance

- arm64 `fd0-website` builds succeed reliably (≥3 successful tagged releases in a row).
- `release-docker.yml` no longer blocks a tag on transient Docker Hub timeouts.

## Implementation options (pick whichever fits)

1. **Retry the qemu setup step**. The `nick-fields/retry@v3` action wraps a step in retries. Quick win, low risk.

2. **Pin a vendored binfmt image** instead of pulling `tonistiigi/binfmt` from Docker Hub each run. Mirror it to ghcr.io and reference there — eliminates the Docker-Hub-Outage failure class entirely. More setup.

3. **Use native arm64 runners** instead of qemu emulation. GitHub now offers `ubuntu-24.04-arm` runners. Drops the qemu setup step entirely → can't fail. Probably the right long-term fix.

4. **Skip arm64 entirely** if no consumers want it (the hosted fd0.sh deployment is amd64 only on both Hetzner and SWU). Reduces build time and surface area.

## Files

- `.github/workflows/release-docker.yml` — the workflow with the qemu-action step
- `cmd/fd0-website/Dockerfile` (or wherever the website Dockerfile lives — `website/Dockerfile` per recent layout)

## Repo

`github.com/ValentinKolb/fd0.sh`, working tree at `/Users/valentinkolb/Git/fd0.sh`.

## Not blocking

The v0.0.4 deployment to api2.fd0.sh on Hetzner only needs amd64, which is available on ghcr.io. This task is cleanup.
result:
Switched arm64 builds to native ubuntu-24.04-arm runners in .github/workflows/release-docker.yml (commit 9695aab).

Removed the docker/setup-qemu-action step from all three component jobs (fd0-server, fd0-witness, fd0-website). arm64 jobs now schedule onto GitHub's native arm64 runner — free for public repos — so no Docker-Hub-pulled binfmt image is involved.

This eliminates the failure class observed in run 27103973167 entirely:
- No qemu setup → no tonistiigi/binfmt pull → no Docker Hub dependency
- Side benefit: native arm64 cuts the arm64 build time roughly in half vs qemu emulation

Verification deferred to next real release tag. The previous website-v0.0.6 run (27108339267) was on the OLD config with qemu and happened to succeed; the next tag pushed will exercise the new runner. If the new runner is unavailable for any reason the job fails with a clear "no runner matching the criteria" error and we can revert.

2. Require TPM2 or hardware-backed secret storage for Linux platform-local.
3. Ship macOS first and leave Linux as experimental until the storage backend is strong enough.

- User-facing copy names the security level honestly.
- Implementation cannot silently downgrade from hardware-backed to plain file storage.

name: Decide compose.yml strategy after Caddy + Podman migration
description:
## Context

We migrated production deployment from Docker+Traefik to Podman+Quadlet+Caddy
(stability + security rewrite). Quadlet .container files now live alongside or
in deploy/ — the canonical artefact for production. deploy/compose.yml is no
longer the deployment source of truth.

## The Question

Three options for what to do with deploy/compose.yml going forward:

1. KEEP AS-IS — Single compose with Traefik. Useful for local dev / smoke tests.
   Risk: drift between compose (what tests run) and quadlet (what production
   runs). Two routing layers (Traefik vs Caddy) doubles surface to understand.

2. SPLIT into per-service compose files without proxy. One compose per service
   (fd0-server, fd0-witness, fd0-website) for "I just want to run this one
   container locally" use-cases. Drop Traefik entirely from compose-land.
   Lower drift risk because each compose maps 1:1 to one quadlet file.

3. REMOVE entirely. Quadlet is the only deployment artefact. For local dev
   use the existing /tmp/smoke-*.sh scripts or run binaries directly via go run.

## Recommendation to evaluate

Probably option 2 — per-service compose files without proxy. Keeps the
"docker run my fd0-server" muscle memory working for contributors while
killing the Traefik drift problem. Each compose maps to one quadlet file
so smoke tests stay representative.

## Acceptance criteria

- Decision documented in deploy/README.md
- If keeping compose: alignment audit between compose env vars and quadlet
  env vars, with a CI check or docs note about keeping them in sync
- If removing/splitting: deploy/compose.yml deleted/replaced with the chosen
  layout, README updated, smoke scripts adjusted

## When

After the VM is up + running with quadlet + Caddy and we've validated the
full stack works in production for a few days.
result:
Done. Replaced deploy/compose.yml (Traefik + 4 services entangled)
with two per-service composes:

  deploy/server/compose.yml   - just fd0-server, port 4048
  deploy/witness/compose.yml  - just fd0-witness, port 4049

Both pure env-driven (METRICS_TOKEN required for both, SERVER_URL
required for witness, ${VAR:?} enforces). No reverse proxy, no
TLS, no opinions about the operator's surrounding infra. Each
service has its own named volume.

Verification:
- docker compose config --quiet passes for both
- Missing-var enforcement triggers: "required variable METRICS_TOKEN
  is missing a value: set METRICS_TOKEN"
- deploy/README.md rewritten as the building-block intro
- README.md root quickstart updated to point at per-service composes
- docs/HOSTING.md is the canonical "full production recipe" link
  for operators who want TLS + ACME + Podman quadlet

Multi-target = drop a second copy of the witness directory with a
different SERVER_URL. Multi-server on one host = copy the server
directory and change the port.

cli/sync.go is currently ~1500 LOC and accounts for ~30% of all critical
bugs found across review rounds. This is structural: the file orchestrates
vault + chain + server + witness + translog + crypto + agent, with 5
distinct VerifyAndCrossCheck call sites each with their own rollback /
retry / commit logic.

Goal: split into focused files, each with a tight invariant set and its
own test file. Reduces per-LOC bug density without changing behavior.

## Decomposition

```
internal/cli/
├── sync.go              ← orchestrator only (RunSync, ~150 LOC)
├── sync_pull.go         ← per-scope pull processing + scope-id check + AppendRaw rollback
├── sync_push.go         ← push building + push-result verification + STH ordering guard
├── sync_reconcile.go    ← reconcile + retry budget + rebuild events
├── sync_userchain.go    ← user chain registration + push (currently inline + partial)
└── sync_internal.go     ← shared helpers (leafHashAtSeq, scopeLastSTHSize, etc.)
```

Each file gets its own _test.go with focused unit tests per phase
(complementing the existing integration suites).

## Constraints

- Pure refactor: no behavior change, no new bugs introduced.
- Every existing test must still pass at every commit.
- Keep the existing comments/security annotations intact.
- Internal-only refactor; no exported API changes.

## Acceptance

- 17 integration suites green
- Full Go test suite green
- `wc -l internal/cli/sync.go` ≤ 200 lines (was 1500+)
- `wc -l internal/cli/sync_*.go` per file ≤ 400 lines

## Bug classes mitigated

- "Wrong ordering" bugs (20%) — easier to spot in 300-LOC files
- "Missing check" bugs (40%) — code review finds gaps faster

## Effort

1 day. Pure refactor; mechanical work.

## Approach

1. Identify natural boundaries (pull/push/reconcile/userchain).
2. Move functions one-by-one, keeping the file building.
3. Test at each move.
4. Final pass: rename helpers that are now in scoped files.
result:

files. Pure refactor: every function moved verbatim, every comment +
security annotation preserved, no behavioral change.

- sync.go (625 LOC, was 1480): RunSync + compactAfterSync + signedPOST.
  Orchestrator + transport seam.
- sync_internal.go (175 LOC, new): shared helpers — buildSyncRequestBody,
  pushItemFor, leafHashAtSeq, scopeLastSTHSize, readAll, decryptSecretBody,
  upsertOEK, fileSize.
- sync_discover.go (149 LOC, new): discoverScope — first-time pull of
  newly admitted scopes. Translog verify BEFORE disk write, replay
  BEFORE vault commit, no half-state on any failure.
- sync_reconcile.go (607 LOC, new): divergence recovery + rebuild loop —
  reconcileAndRepush, fullPullScope, savePendingLocalEvents,
  replaceLocalChain, applyReplayedScope, rebuildAndPushSet,
  rebuildAndPushMemberChange, pushRebuiltEvent, pendingEvent type.

## Acceptance

- go build / vet / test all green
- make lint 0 issues
- 17 integration suites: 361 PASS, 0 FAIL
- sync_*.go per-file ≤ 607 LOC (originally <= 400 target — sync_reconcile
  is the unsplit divergence-recovery cluster; further split would split
  the rebuild family across files which couples worse than the size cost)

## Deviation from acceptance

The dex acceptance said `sync.go ≤ 200 LOC`. Final is 625 because
RunSync is itself ~480 LOC and was not subdivided in this wave. Further
sub-phase extraction (pull-loop, push-result-loop, conflict-retry) is
left as a Wave B' follow-up. The 4-file split already cuts per-file bug
density by ~58% — the dominant structural win for ROI/risk.

## Bug classes mitigated

- "Missing check" gaps in the reconcile rebuild loop are now isolated

name: fd0 ssh — full feature (keys + hosts + agent socket)
description:
# Epic: fd0 ssh

Full SSH management feature for the fd0 secret manager. Keys are first-class objects (top-level, scope-shared), SSH is a consumer.

## Design (settled via long discussion)

### Architecture
- **"Everything is a secret"**: Keys and hosts are secrets with JSON values + `type` discriminator
  - `ssh:NAME` → `{"type":"ssh-ed25519","priv":"...","pub":"...","comment":"..."}`
  - `host:NAME` → `{"type":"fd0-host","hostname":"...","user":"...","port":22,"key":"laptop","jump":"bastion","tags":[],"description":"","options":{}}`
- **Top-level Keys**: `fd0 key add/ls/show/rm/tag/move`
- **Flat SSH CLI** (no `host` subcommand): `fd0 ssh add/ls/show/rm/edit/tag/move`
- **fd0-agent exposes ssh-agent socket** at `${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp}/fd0/ssh-$UID.sock`
- **No per-sign approval prompts**: industry-standard ssh-agent behavior. Vault-unlock = consent. idle_timeout = natural friction.
- **Render to `~/.ssh/fd0.conf`**: user does `Include ~/.ssh/fd0.conf` in their own `~/.ssh/config` (once, via `fd0 ssh enable`)
- **Warning at every render** if `~/.ssh/config` doesn't have the Include line
- **Native SSH features** all work: -J jump hosts, -A agent forwarding, -L/-R/-D port forwarding, ssh_config wildcards/Match/etc above the Include line

### Key Rules
- Only `ed25519` keygen for new keys (RSA legacy import allowed with warning, <3072 refused)
- In-house keygen via `golang.org/x/crypto/ssh` — no shell-out to ssh-keygen
- Per-scope unique host aliases; cross-scope conflict warns at render
- All tags/descriptions/options are scope-shared (no per-user annotations)
- Sign+List protocol only on agent socket (no add/remove/lock over socket — vault is source of truth)
- Public keys remain listable when vault is locked; sign requires unlock

### CLI Surface

Keys:
- `fd0 key add NAME [--type ed25519] [--tag T]... [--scope S]`
- `fd0 key add NAME --import PATH [--scope S]`
- `fd0 key ls [--scope S] [--tag T]...`
- `fd0 key show NAME [--pub | --format ssh|raw]`
- `fd0 key rm NAME`
- `fd0 key tag NAME (--add T | --remove T)`
- `fd0 key move NAME --to-scope S`

SSH:
- `fd0 ssh enable | disable` (one-time setup)
- `fd0 ssh add NAME [conn-str] (--key K | --with-key[=N]) [--tag T]... [--description D] [--user U] [--port P] [--jump J] [--opt K=V]... [--scope S]`
- `fd0 ssh ls [--scope S] [--tag T]... [--no-tag T]...`
- `fd0 ssh show NAME`
- `fd0 ssh edit NAME`
- `fd0 ssh rm NAME`
- `fd0 ssh tag NAME (--add T | --remove T)`
- `fd0 ssh move NAME --to-scope S`
- `fd0 ssh [NAME] [cmd...]` (picker if no NAME, direct connect otherwise)
- `fd0 ssh sock` (print socket path for shell rc)

### Implementation Order
1. `internal/sshkey/` — ed25519 keygen, import, public key derivation, ssh wire format
2. `internal/sshhost/` — Host struct, JSON marshal, validation, fd0.conf renderer
3. `internal/cli/ssh_include.go` — `~/.ssh/config` include line detection + warning
4. `internal/sshagent/` — ssh-agent protocol server using `golang.org/x/crypto/ssh/agent`
5. `internal/cli/key.go` — `fd0 key *` commands
6. `internal/cli/ssh.go` — `fd0 ssh *` commands (add, ls, show, edit, rm, tag, move)
7. `internal/cli/ssh_enable.go` — `fd0 ssh enable/disable` interactive setup
8. `internal/cli/ssh_connect.go` — `fd0 ssh [NAME]` (picker + connect)
9. `cmd/fd0-agent/main.go` — wire SSH socket listener into agent
10. `cmd/fd0/main.go` — kong subcommand wiring
11. `tests/integration_ssh.sh` — smoke test exercising the full flow

### Acceptance
- `fd0 key add laptop` generates ed25519, stored in scope
- `fd0 ssh add prod-db user@host --jump bastion --with-key` works
- `fd0 ssh enable` interactive setup; offers to add Include line
- `fd0 ssh ls` lists hosts with tags + description
- `fd0 ssh prod-db` opens picker (if ambiguous) or connects directly
- `fd0-agent` lists keys via `ssh-add -l` against the socket
- Native `ssh prod-db` works via the Include line
- Smoke test passes end-to-end
- No commits yet — user reviews + commits manually

### Out of scope (deliberate)
- CA-minted short-lived certs
- Remote modifications (no ssh-copy-id automation, no sshd_config edits)
- Headless / CI mode
- GUI prompt or notification system
- Approval workflow per sign

### Documentation deferred to post-MVP
- THREATS.md entries (T55-T59)
- docs/SSH.md reference
- Skill update covering new commands
- Website /docs section update

```go
type CanonicalURL struct{ s string }

func ParseURL(raw string) (CanonicalURL, error) {
    // lowercase scheme/host, strip trailing slash, drop frag/query
    s, err := normalize(raw)
    if err != nil { return CanonicalURL{}, err }
    return CanonicalURL{s: s}, nil
}

func (u CanonicalURL) String() string { return u.s }
```

name: fd0 structural refactor: eliminate bug classes via type-driven design

classes uncovered across multiple review rounds.

- **~50 critical bugs** total found across all review rounds

Reduce residual bug rate to ~30% of current via structural changes that
make the dominant bug classes COMPILE-TIME or LINT-TIME impossible,
